The present petition has been filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 against the impugned order dated 03.08.2024, passed by Learned Additional Sessions Judge,
Pendra Road, District Bilaspur, in Criminal Revision No. 13 of VEDPRAKASH 2024, whereby the criminal revision filed by the petitioner has been DEWANGAN dismissed.

Additional Sessions Judge,
Pendra Road, District Bilaspur

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the case are that the present petitioner is an accused in the offence of Crime No.
38 of 2023 registered at Police Station Gaurella, District Gaurella-Pendra-Marwahi for the offence under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC.

The complainant/Hari Prasad Kashyap has lodged the report to the police with the allegation that on 07.12.2022, two persons came to his house and informed him that they came from Indus Company and came to install a tower in his house.

They took the complainant to Amarkantak and taken Rs.15 lakh cash in a bag and by kept him in assurance that the bag, which they were having contains with a diamond and fled away along with the cash amount.
During the investigation, Rs. 3,15,000/- have been seized from the bank account of the present petitioner.

sentences.text: After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed before the Learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Pendra Road and the Criminal Case No. 336 of 2023 is pending against him.
In the criminal case, the petitioner had filed an application on 24.04.2024 under Section 451 of Cr.P.C. for grant of interim custody of the seized amount of Rs. 3,15,000/-.

It is submitted by the petitioner before the Learned Judicial Magistrate First Class that the said amount was of his own amount,
which comes through sale of paddy and it is not the subject matter of the offence, therefore, the same may be given to him in interim custody.

After hearing the parties, the Learned Trial Court has passed the order on 26.04.2024 dismissing his application by holding that Rs. 3,15,500/- was seized by the police from the present petitioner on his memorandum and the ownership of the subject cash amount is the subject matter of the offence, which can only be decided after the trial, hence the application of the petitioner was dismissed.

The said order dated 26.04.2024 was challenged by the petitioner before the Learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Pendra Road by filing a Criminal Revision No. 13 of 2024 and after hearing the parties, the Learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge,
Pendra Road has also dismissed the criminal revision filed by the petitioner vide order dated 03.08.2024 by saying that, since there are conflicting claims over the subject property and therefore at this stage it cannot be presumed that the petitioner is the owner of the subject property.
The said order dated 03.08.2024 is under challenge in the present petition.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the cash amount of Rs. 3,15,000/- has been seized from the petitioner, who is an accused and legally entitled for the said amount.
The source of said amount was the sale of his paddy and he kept the amount in his bank account, but the police has seized the said amount considering that it is the subject matter of the offence.

He would further submit that while he was in custody, the said amount was withdrawn from the bank, which itself shows that it was the petitioner's amount, which was withdrawn from District Co-operative Central Bank, Baikunthpur branch and therefore, the said amount may be given to the petitioner in interim custody.

5. Learned counsel for the State opposes the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and supported the impugned orders passed by Learned Trial Court as well as Revisional Court.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents annexed with the petition.

7. From perusal of the impugned order dated 03.08.2024, it appears that the Learned Revisional Court has elaborately considered the merits of the case and has come into conclusion that there is rival claims of the complainant as well as the accused/petitioner over the subject property of Rs.
3,15,000/-.

The claim of the complainant is that the accused persons conspired together and cheated Rs. 15 lakhs from him, whereas the claim of the petitioner/accused is that the said amount of Rs. 3,15,000/- is the amount of sale of his paddy.
The source of their claim are obviously to be decided after the trial and at this stage, it cannot be presumed that the amount seized in the case belongs to the accused/petitioner or the complainant.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the Learned Trial Court as well as the Revisional Court have not committed any illegality in rejecting the application of the petitioner for grant of interim custody of the seized amount.
